blocks.text: Cache generated content by version and refresh evidence per customer without overwriting review choices. Bound rendered rows while keeping the approval summary and unresolved outcomes reachable.

blocks.title: Failures and truthful UI
rows: Generated response is slow or malformed
Keep the request retryable and reject invalid structure
The account list remains usable; no approval control appears for invalid content
Refresh only affected evidence and mark reviewed edits for another look
Old and current values are identified without clearing the whole review
The row explains the denial and can be removed from the pending command
OutcomeReducer retains one status and audit event per customer
Successes, conflicts, denials, and failures have separate next actions
Retry lookup with the same command identity
The interface recovers the existing outcome instead of submitting duplicate edits

steps.title: Record the request
steps.text: Disable repeated Cancel clicks, create one cancelCommandId, and label the execution as cancellation requested rather than canceled.

steps.title: Continue reconciliation
steps.text: Keep listening for ActionOutcome or fetch it after reconnect because stopping the local request does not settle remote work.

steps.title: Accept the late truth
steps.text: If two records succeeded and one failed after Cancel, show those results and note that the cancellation request arrived too late for the successes.

steps.title: Offer compensating recovery
steps.text: Create a separate rollback command only for confirmed successes with valid rollback tokens, current permission, and unchanged customer versions.

blocks.text: Rollback never edits the original ActionOutcome. Its own per-item result records which customer stages were restored, which now conflict, and which are no longer reversible. This preserves a readable audit chain from proposal through approval, execution, cancel intent, and compensation.

blocks.alt: Timeline of a cancellation request racing with late lifecycle-stage results before a separate rollback command is offered.
blocks.caption: Cancel expresses intent; a late authoritative outcome decides whether compensating rollback is available.
blocks.fallbackText: Text fallback: The specialist requests cancellation while execution is active. A late outcome confirms two successes and one failure. The UI preserves all three results, marks cancellation as too late for completed work, and offers rollback only for reversible successes.

blocks.text: Use a stable reading order, visible row labels, and text rather than color alone for freshness and outcomes. Announce proposal readiness, approval acceptance, and the final mixed result concisely; do not announce every generated token or row refresh. Keep focus near the triggering control. On narrow screens, evidence and recovery controls stack beneath the customer name without hiding the selected count or approval summary.

Release proposal and evidence review before mutation. Add reversible approvals, then expand after audit and support review. Track removals, overrides, stale evidence, permission denials, mixed outcomes, cancel races, rollback conflicts, and recovery time by record count, transition risk, input, assistive technology, and viewport.
